name: Clock Period Decreased
description: A clock period was reduced (frequency increased).
why_matters: Higher frequency tightens all timing paths: may cause setup violations.
fix: Verify the new frequency is achievable for the design.

name: Clock Period Increased
description: A clock period was increased (frequency decreased).
why_matters: Lower frequency relaxes timing: paths previously analyzed at higher frequency may have excess margin.
fix: Verify the frequency reduction is intentional.

name: Clock Added
description: A new create_clock appeared in V2.
why_matters: New clocks add timing domains: may require new CDC constraints.
fix: Add corresponding set_clock_groups, I/O delays, and uncertainty for the new clock.

name: Clock Removed
description: A create_clock from V1 was removed in V2.
why_matters: Removed clocks eliminate a timing domain: associated constraints become orphaned.
fix: Remove or update any constraints that reference the deleted clock.

name: Clock Port Changed
description: A create_clock source port changed between V1 and V2.
why_matters: Changing the clock port means the clock is now on a different physical pin: all I/O delays and CDC constraints may be wrong.
fix: Verify the new port is correct and update all related constraints.

name: Derate Value Changed
description: A set_timing_derate value changed between V1 and V2.
why_matters: Changed derate values alter timing margins across the design: may cause or hide violations.
fix: Verify the new derate is appropriate for the target corner.

name: Derate Direction Changed
description: A derate shifted from -early to -late or vice versa.
why_matters: Swapping derate direction completely reverses the timing impact: setup becomes hold and vice versa.
fix: Verify the direction is correct for the intended analysis.

name: False Path Removed
description: A set_false_path from V1 was removed in V2.
why_matters: Removed false paths cause the tool to analyze previously-excluded paths, often leading to timing violations.
fix: Restore the false path or verify the path is truly no longer false.

name: False Path Target Changed
description: A set_false_path -from/-to/-through changed between V1 and V2.
why_matters: Changed false path targets may leave real paths un-excluded while excluding different paths.
fix: Verify both the old and new false path targets are correct.

name: False Path Added
description: A new set_false_path appeared in V2.
why_matters: New false paths reduce timing analysis coverage: verify the path is genuinely false.
fix: Review the new false path to ensure it doesn't mask real violations.

name: New Constraint Added
description: A new SDC constraint appeared in V2 that wasn't in V1.
why_matters: New constraints add timing restrictions that weren't previously checked.
fix: Review the new constraint to ensure it's correct and necessary.

name: Constraint Removed
description: An SDC constraint from V1 was removed in V2.
why_matters: Removed constraints relax timing analysis: paths previously constrained may now be unconstrained.
fix: Verify the removal is intentional and doesn't leave timing gaps.

name: Constraint Modified
description: An SDC constraint text changed between V1 and V2 (not covered by specific rules above).
why_matters: Review the modification to ensure it's correct.
fix: Compare V1 and V2 text to understand the change.

name: I/O Delay Changed
description: A set_input_delay or set_output_delay value changed.
why_matters: Changed I/O delays alter timing margins at port boundaries.
fix: Verify the new delay matches the interface specification.

name: Multicycle Setup Decreased
description: A multicycle -setup N was changed to a smaller value.
why_matters: Reduced setup cycles tighten timing: paths that previously met timing may now fail.
fix: Verify the new multicycle value is correct for the data protocol.

name: Multicycle Hold Decreased
description: A multicycle -hold N was changed to a smaller value.
why_matters: Reduced hold cycles tighten hold analysis: may cause false hold violations.
fix: Verify the hold multicycle matches the setup multicycle (hold = setup - 1).

name: Multicycle Increased
description: A multicycle path cycles count was increased.
why_matters: More relaxed multicycle: previously analyzed paths may no longer be checked at the correct boundary.
fix: Verify the increase is intentional and matches the data protocol.

name: Multicycle Removed
description: A set_multicycle_path from V1 was removed in V2.
why_matters: Removed multicycle paths revert to single-cycle analysis: paths that needed multi-cycle will now fail.
fix: Restore the multicycle path or verify the protocol changed.

name: Operating Condition Changed
description: set_operating_conditions changed between V1 and V2.
why_matters: Different operating conditions mean a different PVT corner: all derate and uncertainty values should be reviewed.
fix: Ensure the new condition matches the intended corner and all related values are updated.

name: Wildcard Pattern Changed
description: A wildcard object filter (get_cells, get_pins, etc.) changed between V1 and V2.
why_matters: Changed wildcards may narrow or broaden the set of affected objects, altering which paths are constrained.
fix: Verify the new pattern matches the intended object set.

name: Wildcard Narrowed
description: A wildcard pattern now matches fewer objects than in V1.
why_matters: Narrowed wildcards leave some previously-constrained objects unconstrained.
fix: Ensure the narrowed pattern still covers all intended objects.

name: Missing Clock Definition
description: No create_clock defined in the SDC file.
why_matters: Without a clock, the synthesis tool has no timing reference: all paths are unconstrained and QoR is meaningless.
fix: Add 'create_clock -name clk -period <ns> [get_ports <port>]' for every clock domain.

name: Duplicate Clock Name
description: Two or more create_clock commands share the same -name value.
why_matters: Duplicate names cause the tool to silently overwrite the first clock definition, leading to wrong timing.
fix: Use unique names for each clock domain, or use -add if multiple clocks on the same port.

name: Generated Clock Missing -source
description: A create_generated_clock command is missing the required -source flag.
why_matters: Without -source the tool cannot determine the master clock edge, producing random divider behavior.
fix: Add '-source [get_ports <port>]' or '-source [get_pins <pin>]' to the create_generated_clock.

name: Conflicting Divide/Multiply
description: A create_generated_clock has both -divide_by and -multiply_by set.
why_matters: These flags are mutually exclusive: using both produces undefined frequency.
fix: Use either -divide_by OR -multiply_by, not both.

name: No Input Delay
description: Clocks are defined but no set_input_delay exists.
why_matters: All input ports are timing-unconstrained: setup/hold at input boundaries is never checked.
fix: Add 'set_input_delay -max <value> [get_ports <port>]' for each input port.

name: No Output Delay
description: Clocks are defined but no set_output_delay exists.
why_matters: All output ports are timing-unconstrained: the tool cannot verify output timing.
fix: Add 'set_output_delay -max <value> [get_ports <port>]' for each output port.

name: Clock on Data Port
description: A create_clock is defined on a port whose name suggests it is a data bus (data, addr, bus, wdata, etc.).
why_matters: Creating a clock on a data port constrains data as a clock, which breaks timing analysis.
fix: Use a dedicated clock port. If this is a data strobe, use set_clock_latency or set_input_delay instead.

name: Input Delay >= Clock Period
description: A set_input_delay value is greater than or equal to the clock period.
why_matters: This leaves zero or negative time for combinational logic: timing closure is mathematically impossible.
fix: Reduce input delay or increase clock period. Check if the delay value is in the correct unit (ns vs ps).

name: Output Delay >= Clock Period
description: A set_output_delay value is greater than or equal to the clock period.
why_matters: Zero margin for output logic means the path can never meet timing.
fix: Reduce output delay or increase clock period.

name: Propagated Clock on Virtual Clock
description: set_propagated_clock is applied to a virtual clock (no source port).
why_matters: Virtual clocks have no physical source: there is nothing to propagate through the network.
fix: Remove set_propagated_clock for virtual clocks, or convert the virtual clock to a real clock with a source port.

name: Invalid Case Analysis Value
description: set_case_analysis has a value other than 0, 1, rising, or falling.
why_matters: The tool only recognizes these four values: anything else causes a parse error or silent ignore.
fix: Use 'set_case_analysis 0', 'set_case_analysis 1', 'set_case_analysis rising', or 'set_case_analysis falling'.

name: Suspicious False Path
description: A set_false_path -from X -to Y does not contain typical async/scan/test keywords.
why_matters: False paths bypass timing analysis: an incorrect false path hides real violations.
fix: Verify the path is genuinely false (async CDC, test mode, etc.). Add a comment explaining why.

name: Multicycle Without Hold Fix
description: A multicycle -setup N path is missing the corresponding -hold (N-1) adjustment.
why_matters: Without the hold fix, the tool checks hold at the original 1-cycle boundary, causing false hold violations.
fix: Add '-hold <N-1>' to match every '-setup N' multicycle path.

name: Unrealistically Tight Uncertainty
description: Clock uncertainty is set below 0.05ns.
why_matters: Overly tight uncertainty causes the tool to over-optimize, producing designs that fail in silicon.
fix: Use a realistic uncertainty value based on PLL jitter + clock tree skew (typically 0.1-0.3ns).

name: Very High Clock Uncertainty
description: Clock uncertainty is set above 0.5ns.
why_matters: High uncertainty wastes timing margin: the tool adds unnecessary buffer insertion, hurting area and power.
fix: Verify the uncertainty value. For most designs, 0.1-0.3ns is appropriate.

name: Multiple Clocks Without Clock Groups
description: Multiple clocks defined but no set_clock_groups command found.
why_matters: Without clock group declarations, the tool analyzes all cross-clock paths as synchronous, missing real CDC issues.
fix: Add 'set_clock_groups -asynchronous -group [get_clocks X] -group [get_clocks Y]' for unrelated clock domains.

name: Wildcard dont_touch
description: set_dont_touch is applied with a wildcard ([all_cells] or *).
why_matters: This blocks ALL optimization, severely degrading QoR (area, timing, power).
fix: Apply dont_touch only to specific cells/nets that need it, not globally.

name: Extremely Tight max_transition
description: set_max_transition is below 0.05ns.
why_matters: Ultra-tight transition constraints cause excessive buffer insertion and may be physically unachievable.
fix: Use a realistic transition target (typically 0.1-0.3ns depending on technology node).

name: set_max_delay Without -datapath_only
description: A set_max_delay constraint is missing -datapath_only.
why_matters: Without this flag, the constraint also affects hold analysis on the same path, potentially causing incorrect results.
fix: Add '-datapath_only' unless you intentionally want to constrain both setup and hold.

name: No Input Delay -min
description: set_input_delay exists but no -min variant.
why_matters: Hold timing at input ports cannot be checked without -min input delay.
fix: Add 'set_input_delay -min <value> [get_ports <port>]' for hold analysis.

name: No Output Delay -min
description: set_output_delay exists but no -min variant.
why_matters: Hold timing at output ports is unconstrained.
fix: Add 'set_output_delay -min <value> [get_ports <port>]' for hold analysis.

name: No set_propagated_clock
description: Clocks are defined but set_propagated_clock is missing.
why_matters: The ideal clock model assumes zero insertion delay and skew: overly optimistic for post-layout correlation.
fix: Add 'set_propagated_clock [all_clocks]' after CTS to model real clock tree delay.

name: Clock Groups Missing Exclusion Type
description: A set_clock_groups command is missing -asynchronous, -logically_exclusive, or -physically_exclusive.
why_matters: Without an exclusion type, the constraint has no effect: cross-clock paths are still analyzed as synchronous.
fix: Add the appropriate flag: -asynchronous (no phase relation), -physically_exclusive (same port), or -logically_exclusive (mux-select).

name: Derate Early Without Late
description: set_timing_derate has -early but no matching -late.
why_matters: Unbalanced derate skews setup vs hold analysis in opposite directions, producing inconsistent results.
fix: Add a matching -late derate value.

name: Derate Late Without Early
description: set_timing_derate has -late but no matching -early.
why_matters: Same issue as SDC-032: asymmetric derate.
fix: Add a matching -early derate value.

name: Data Check Without -clock
description: set_data_check is missing a -clock reference.
why_matters: Without -clock, the tool cannot determine which edge to check against.
fix: Add '-clock [get_clocks <name>]' to the set_data_check command.

name: Excessive Disable Timing
description: More than 5 set_disable_timing commands found.
why_matters: Large numbers of disable_timing arcs can hide real timing violations by disabling critical paths.
fix: Review each disable_timing: ensure they are necessary and not masking real issues.

name: Disable Timing Without From/To
description: A set_disable_timing command is missing both -from and -to.
why_matters: This disables ALL timing arcs on the specified cell: almost always wrong and hides real violations.
fix: Add explicit -from and -to pin specifiers to disable only the intended arc.

name: Half-Cycle Without Hold Fix
description: Half-cycle multicycle paths (-rise_to/-fall_to on -setup) found without matching -hold 0.
why_matters: Hold analysis will be wrong at the half-cycle boundary.
fix: Add '-hold 0' with matching -rise_to/-fall_to for each half-cycle setup path.

name: cell_early Derate < 1.0
description: set_timing_derate -early -cell_delay is below 1.0.
why_matters: Early derate < 1.0 makes cells faster, reducing hold margin: opposite of intended conservative analysis.
fix: Use cell_early > 1.0 (e.g., 1.05) for conservative hold analysis.

name: cell_late Derate > 1.0
description: set_timing_derate -late -cell_delay is above 1.0.
why_matters: Late derate > 1.0 makes cells faster, reducing setup margin; it should be < 1.0 for conservative analysis.
fix: Use cell_late < 1.0 (e.g., 0.95) for conservative setup analysis.

name: net_early Derate < 1.0
description: set_timing_derate -early -net_delay is below 1.0.
why_matters: Early net derate < 1.0 reduces hold margin on interconnect delays.
fix: Use net_early > 1.0 for conservative hold analysis.

name: net_late Derate > 1.0
description: set_timing_derate -late -net_delay is above 1.0.
why_matters: Late net derate > 1.0 reduces setup margin on interconnect delays.
fix: Use net_late < 1.0 for conservative setup analysis.

name: Unrecognized Operating Condition
description: set_operating_conditions name doesn't match common patterns (WORST, BEST, TYP, SSG, TT, FFG, etc.).
why_matters: Non-standard names may indicate a typo or missing library setup.
fix: Verify the condition name matches your library's operating condition definitions.

name: Hold/Setup Uncertainty Ratio
description: Clock uncertainty -hold is not approximately 0.5x of -setup.
why_matters: Hold uncertainty should typically be ~half of setup uncertainty (skew dominates hold). Unusual ratios may indicate a typo.
fix: Review the values: typically -hold ≈ 0.5 * -setup.

name: Undefined Clock in I/O Delay
description: A set_input_delay / set_output_delay -clock names a clock that no create_clock or create_generated_clock defines.
why_matters: Real tools fail or warn on this because the port-to-clock association is broken: the delay would be applied to nothing, and static analysis must NOT silently substitute a different clock.
fix: Fix the -clock name, or add the missing create_clock / create_generated_clock definition.

name: Undefined Master Clock
description: A create_generated_clock -master_clock names a clock that is not defined in this SDC.
why_matters: Without a resolvable master clock the generated clock's period and phase are undefined, making downstream timing meaningless.
fix: Add the create_clock/create_generated_clock that defines the master, or fix the -master_clock name.

name: Undefined Clock in Clock Groups
description: A set_clock_groups -group names a clock that is not defined by any create_clock/create_generated_clock.
why_matters: Grouping a nonexistent clock silently excludes nothing: CDC paths involving it remain unhandled.
fix: Fix the clock name, or define the missing clock first.

name: Contradictory Case Analysis
description: The same pin/port is assigned two different set_case_analysis values in one file (e.g. 0 then 1).
why_matters: A pin cannot be both 0 and 1 in the same mode: the later value silently overrides the earlier, hiding a real conflict.
fix: Use one value per object per mode, or split the modes into separate SDC files.

name: Clock Mismatch Across Corners
description: Clock names or definitions differ between PVT corners.
why_matters: Inconsistent clock definitions cause wrong timing analysis in some corners.
fix: Ensure all corners have matching clock definitions.

name: Clock Period Differs Between Corners
description: Clock periods differ across corners (may be intentional for multi-mode).
why_matters: This is often intentional (e.g., different modes at different frequencies) but should be verified.
fix: Confirm the period differences are intentional multi-mode design.

name: Missing Timing Exceptions in Some Corners
description: A timing exception (false path, multicycle, etc.) exists in some corners but is missing in others.
why_matters: Missing exceptions cause the tool to analyze paths that should be excluded, producing false violations.
fix: Add the missing timing exceptions to all relevant corners.

name: Derate Not Monotonically Ordered
description: Derate values are not monotonically ordered across PVT corners (e.g., worst has lower derate than typical).
why_matters: Non-monotonic derate violates the corner ordering assumption: results from different corners cannot be compared.
fix: Verify derate ordering: worst-case should be most conservative (highest cell_early, lowest cell_late).

name: Design Object Not Found
description: A get_ports/get_pins/get_cells/get_nets reference names an explicit object that does not exist in the supplied design context.
why_matters: Referencing a nonexistent object makes the constraint silently apply to nothing: real timing paths stay unconstrained while the SDC looks correct.
fix: Fix the object name, or add the missing port/pin/cell/net to the design.

name: Empty Collection
description: A wildcard collection (e.g. [get_ports debug_*]) matched nothing in the supplied design context.
why_matters: An empty collection means the constraint applies to zero objects: a typo'd or stale pattern quietly leaves real objects unconstrained.
fix: Verify the wildcard pattern matches at least one design object.

name: Invalid Hierarchy Reference
description: A get_pins/get_cells path references an instance parent that does not exist in the design hierarchy (e.g. u_core/u_nope/D where u_core/u_nope is absent).
why_matters: Invalid hierarchy paths resolve to nothing in the tool: the intended pins/cells are never constrained.
fix: Fix the hierarchical path to match a real instance in the netlist.

name: Top Module Ambiguity
description: The supplied netlist has multiple candidate top modules (or the requested top does not exist): design context could not be built.
why_matters: Without a resolved top module, port-level and hierarchy validation cannot run; ambiguous selection would silently pick the wrong design boundary.
fix: Specify the top module explicitly (--top / UI selector), or add a unique top module.

name: Unconstrained Port
description: A data-pattern input/output port of the supplied design has no set_input_delay/set_output_delay (and is not a clock port).
why_matters: Unconstrained boundary ports leave real interface timing unverified: the design can pass synthesis timing while failing at the chip boundary.
fix: Add set_input_delay/set_output_delay for the port, or explicitly document why it is exempt (clock/reset/control).

name: Async Instead of Physically Exclusive
description: Clock pair marked -asynchronous but should be -physically_exclusive (same source port, different periods).
why_matters: -asynchronous causes unnecessary Crosstalk/SI analysis on paths that can never physically exist simultaneously.
fix: Change to 'set_clock_groups -physically_exclusive' for clocks sharing the same source port.

name: Exclusive But Clocks Are Synchronous
description: Clock pair marked -logically_exclusive or -physically_exclusive but clocks have a real timing relationship (parent-child/synchronous).
why_matters: This masks real setup/hold timing paths, leaving them un-optimized, which can cause silicon failure.
fix: Remove the set_clock_groups for synchronous clocks (parent-child or same-master relationships don't need exclusion).

name: Missing Clock Relationship
description: An asynchronous or physically exclusive clock pair has no set_clock_groups entry.
why_matters: Without explicit grouping, the tool may analyze cross-domain paths as synchronous (over-constraining).
fix: Add 'set_clock_groups -asynchronous -group [get_clocks X] -group [get_clocks Y]'.

name: Wrong Exclusion Type
description: Clock pair marked with an exclusion type (-logically_exclusive or -physically_exclusive) but appears to be asynchronous.
why_matters: Using exclusion instead of -asynchronous may be overly restrictive or indicate a design intent mismatch.
fix: Verify the exclusion type is intentional. Use -asynchronous for unrelated clock domains.

name: Unconstrained Data Input (structural)
description: An input port whose net structurally drives instance data pins (D/DIN/DATA) has no set_input_delay.
why_matters: The port is structurally a data boundary, so its external setup/hold is genuinely unconstrained: this is stronger evidence than a name-based guess.
fix: Add set_input_delay (-max/-min) for the port, or verify the port is intentionally exempt.

name: Unconstrained Data Output (structural)
description: An output port whose net is structurally driven by instance data pins (Q/DOUT) has no set_output_delay.
why_matters: The port is structurally a data output boundary, so its external setup/hold is genuinely unconstrained.
fix: Add set_output_delay (-max/-min) for the port, or verify the port is intentionally exempt.

name: Partially Constrained Bus
description: A bus port has I/O delay on only some of its bits (provable from the SDC collections), leaving the other bits unconstrained.
why_matters: Partial bus coverage means some bits of the interface have no external timing constraint: a subtle gap that full-interface constraint reviews exist to catch.
fix: Constrain the whole bus (e.g. [get_ports data_in]) or explicitly constrain every bit.

name: Exact Duplicate Constraint
description: The same normalized constraint (same command, objects, options, value) is issued more than once.
why_matters: The second command is a no-op: the constraint already exists. Harmless but redundant; often a copy-paste artifact.
fix: Remove the duplicate, or keep it only if a comment explains why it is intentional.

name: Overridden Constraint
description: A later constraint with the same objects/clock/edge but a different value silently replaces an earlier one (no -add_delay).
why_matters: The earlier constraint is dead: if the override is unintentional, the intended timing value is silently lost.
fix: Verify the override is intentional, or use -add_delay if both values should accumulate.

name: Contradictory Max/Min Delay
description: set_max_delay value is smaller than set_min_delay on provably identical endpoints.
why_matters: A timing window where max < min is impossible: no path can satisfy both required_max < required_min. This is provable without STA.
fix: Fix the values so set_max_delay >= set_min_delay on the same endpoints.

name: Timing Exception Interaction
description: A set_false_path and a set_multicycle_path/set_max_delay/set_min_delay reference overlapping endpoint objects.
why_matters: Object overlap is NOT proof that the same timing path is affected: the exact interaction requires STA/path analysis. A false path may legally coexist with an exception on different edge/phase combinations.
fix: Review the exceptions with STA to confirm whether the same path is both false and constrained.

name: Missing sdc_version
description: No 'set sdc_version' declaration found.
why_matters: Tool version compatibility may be affected without an explicit version declaration.
fix: Add 'set sdc_version 2.2' at the top of the SDC file.

name: Missing set_units
description: No set_units declaration found.
why_matters: Without explicit units, different tools may interpret numeric values differently (ns vs ps).
fix: Add 'set_units -time ns -capacitance pF'.

name: Missing set_max_fanout
description: No set_max_fanout constraint.
why_matters: Unconstrained fanout can create high-capacity nets that slow down transitions.
fix: Add 'set_max_fanout 20 [all_inputs]' (adjust for your technology).

name: Missing set_max_transition
description: No set_max_transition constraint.
why_matters: Unconstrained slew can cause signal integrity issues and increased dynamic power.
fix: Add 'set_max_transition 0.2 [all_nets]' (adjust for your technology).

name: Missing set_max_capacitance
description: No set_max_capacitance constraint.
why_matters: Unconstrained capacitance affects signal integrity and power.
fix: Add 'set_max_capacitance 0.5 [all_nets]' (adjust for your technology).

name: Missing set_load
description: No set_load on output ports.
why_matters: Without output load, the tool optimizes for zero fanout: unrealistic for real interconnect.
fix: Add 'set_load 0.05 [get_ports <output>]' based on expected board trace capacitance.

name: Missing Driving Cell / Input Transition
description: No set_driving_cell, set_input_transition, or set_drive on input ports.
why_matters: Ideal input slew is overly optimistic: real drivers have finite output impedance.
fix: Add 'set_driving_cell -cell <cell> [all_inputs]' or 'set_input_transition 0.1 [all_inputs]'.

name: Missing Clock Latency
description: No set_clock_latency defined.
why_matters: Without source latency, the tool assumes the clock arrives at the chip boundary with zero delay.
fix: Add 'set_clock_latency -source <value> [all_clocks]' for off-chip clock insertion delay.

name: Missing Clock Transition
description: No set_clock_transition defined.
why_matters: Ideal clock transition (zero slew) is unrealistic and affects clock gating check accuracy.
fix: Add 'set_clock_transition 0.1 [all_clocks]' based on PLL output characteristics.

name: Missing set_case_analysis
description: No set_case_analysis for DFT/test signals.
why_matters: Without case_analysis, DFT paths (scan_en, test_mode) dominate timing analysis.
fix: Add 'set_case_analysis 0 [get_ports scan_en]' (or 1) to fix DFT signal values.

name: Missing set_ideal_network
description: No set_ideal_network to mark reset/scan as ideal.
why_matters: Reset and scan signals modeled as real nets waste optimization effort on non-functional paths.
fix: Add 'set_ideal_network [get_nets rst_n scan_en]' for pre-CTS reset/scan networks.

name: Excessive False Paths
description: More than 10 set_false_path commands found.
why_matters: Large numbers of false paths may indicate overly broad exclusions that hide real violations.
fix: Audit each false path to ensure it is genuinely false. Consider using set_clock_groups instead.

name: Excessive Multicycle Paths
description: More than 8 set_multicycle_path commands found.
why_matters: Many multicycle paths suggest complex timing protocols: each one needs documentation.
fix: Document each multicycle path with a comment explaining the data protocol.

name: Missing set_dont_use
description: No set_dont_use constraint.
why_matters: Without dont_use, the tool may use weak or problematic cells (e.g., low-Vt, clock buffers on data paths).
fix: Add 'set_dont_use [get_lib_cells <lib>/dont_use_cell]' to exclude problematic cells.

name: Missing Operating Conditions
description: No set_operating_conditions defined.
why_matters: Without explicit PVT corner, the tool uses library defaults, which may not match the target corner.
fix: Add 'set_operating_conditions -max <corner_name>' for the target PVT.

name: Missing set_timing_derate
description: No set_timing_derate defined.
why_matters: Without derate, the tool uses nominal delays: insufficient for AOCV/POCVM advanced signoff.
fix: Add set_timing_derate values for cell and net early/late delays.

name: Missing set_clock_jitter
description: No set_clock_jitter defined.
why_matters: Random jitter is not modeled separately from uncertainty, so timing may be over or under-constrained.
fix: Add 'set_clock_jitter <value> [get_clocks <name>]' based on PLL specifications.

name: Missing group_path
description: No group_path defined.
why_matters: Without path grouping, synthesis optimizes all paths equally: critical interfaces may not get priority.
fix: Add 'group_path -name <name> -from <start> -to <end> -weight <N>' for critical paths.

name: Missing set_clock_gating_check
description: No set_clock_gating_check defined.
why_matters: If the design uses clock gating cells, the tool won't check setup/hold on gating pin without this.
fix: Add 'set_clock_gating_check -setup 0.0 -hold 0.0 [all_clocks]' or target specific gating cells.

name: Disable Timing Present
description: set_disable_timing commands found in the SDC.
why_matters: Disable_timing arcs hide timing paths: verify each is intentional and not masking real violations.
fix: Review each set_disable_timing with -from/-to pin specificity.

name: set_min_delay Present
description: set_min_delay constraints found.
why_matters: min_delay can conflict with hold constraints: verify no overlap.
fix: Check that set_min_delay and set_multicycle_path -hold don't target the same paths.

name: Missing Wire Load Constraints
description: No set_wire_load_mode or set_wire_load_model defined.
why_matters: Without wire load, interconnect delay is estimated with default models, which may not match the physical layout.
fix: Add wire load constraints for pre-layout synthesis, or remove if using wireload-free flow.

name: Missing set_max_area
description: No set_max_area constraint.
why_matters: Without area target, synthesis optimizes only timing, potentially producing oversized designs.
fix: Add 'set_max_area <value>' to constrain total cell area.

name: Missing Power Constraints
description: No set_max_dynamic_power or set_max_leakage_power defined.
why_matters: Without power constraints, synthesis ignores power optimization.
fix: Add 'set_max_dynamic_power <value>' and/or 'set_max_leakage_power <value>' for power-aware synthesis.

name: Clock Gating Without Min Pulse Width
description: set_clock_gating_check is present but no set_min_pulse_width.
why_matters: Narrow pulses may trigger clock gating cells incorrectly: min_pulse_width prevents glitches.
fix: Add 'set_min_pulse_width <value> [get_clocks <name>]' to prevent narrow-pulse triggering.

name: Voltage Without Voltage Area
description: set_voltage found but no create_voltage_area.
why_matters: set_voltage without a voltage area has no effect: the voltage domain is undefined.
fix: Add 'create_voltage_area -region <name> [get_ports <port>]' to define the voltage domain.

name: Virtual Clocks Detected
description: Virtual clocks (no source port) are defined.
why_matters: Virtual clocks model off-chip interfaces: ensure I/O delay constraints reference them correctly.
fix: Verify set_input_delay/set_output_delay uses -clock [get_clocks <virtual_clk>].

name: Operating Conditions Without Corner Context
description: set_operating_conditions found but no corner/mode comments in the file.
why_matters: Without comments, it's unclear which PVT corner this SDC targets.
fix: Add comments like '# Corner: WORST, SS/0.9V/125C' near the set_operating_conditions.

name: Multiple Operating Conditions
description: Multiple set_operating_conditions commands found in one file.
why_matters: Multiple conditions in one file may indicate a copy-paste error or incorrect multi-corner setup.
fix: Each SDC file should typically have one set_operating_conditions for its target corner.

name: Derate Without Operating Conditions
description: set_timing_derate found but no set_operating_conditions.
why_matters: Derate values are corner-specific: without operating conditions, the corner context is unclear.
fix: Add set_operating_conditions or a comment identifying the target corner.

name: Clock Relation Analysis Skipped
description: The clock relation analyzer failed to run (likely an import or parse error).
why_matters: Clock relation checks (SDC-060..063) were not performed: potential issues may be missed.
fix: Check that clock_relations.py is importable and the SDC text is valid.

name: Timing Exception Without Rationale Comment
description: A set_false_path / set_multicycle_path / set_case_analysis line has no substantive explanatory comment within the 3 lines above or inline.
why_matters: An undocumented timing exception can hide a real violation: a later engineer cannot tell whether the path is genuinely false (async CDC, test mode) or was silently exempted.
fix: Add a comment above the line or inline (e.g. '# async CDC: two-flop synchronizer, no timing path') explaining why the exception is correct.

name: Unconstrained Reset Tree
description: A net structurally driving >= 2 flip-flop reset pins (RESET-class instance pins) has no timing exception touching it.
why_matters: An async reset tree with no exception leaves the deassertion path and CDC paths unconstrained: silent false hold violations or missed CDC analysis.
fix: Add a targeted exception, e.g. set_false_path -from [get_ports <reset>] -to [all_registers], or set_ideal_network on the reset net, and verify the reset synchronizer input.

name: Suspect Blanket False Path
description: A wildcard set_false_path (all_inputs / * / all_ports) provably covers a reset tree while no targeted exception exists.
why_matters: A blanket false path hides the sync-input vs deassertion distinction that an async-reset synchronizer requires: the mechanism is never actually verified.
fix: Replace the blanket cut with a targeted set_false_path on the reset net (or -through its synchronizer), and consider whether set_clock_groups -asynchronous is masking CDC paths.

name: Reset Synchronizer Input Unconstrained
description: A reset tree whose net also drives data input(s), the structural shape of an async-reset synchronizer sync stage, has no exception.
why_matters: The synchronizer's sync input and the deassertion path need distinct handling, not one blanket false path; a blanket exception silently ignores the difference.
fix: Constrain the synchronizer input and the deassertion path separately (e.g. a targeted false path on the sync flops' D pins, and a separate one on the reset deassertion).

name: Scan Enable Without Mode Coverage
description: A scan_en / scan_enable / test_mode-style signal is referenced in the SDC (proving the design is DFT) but has NO set_case_analysis mode assignment, or only a non-mode value (rising/falling).
why_matters: Without case analysis for every mode, STA blends shift-timing and capture-timing paths into one report: a silent, specific DFT failure. A single-value assignment (0 or 1) is legitimate per-mode practice.
fix: Add set_case_analysis 0 [get_ports <sig>] (function/capture) and set_case_analysis 1 [get_ports <sig>] (scan shift): or verify each mode is constrained in its own corner file.

name: Scan False Path Too Broad
description: A fully-blanket set_false_path (both -from and -to sides all_*/wildcard) in a DFT design, and when a netlist is present, a cut matching all flops while the design shows a scan-chain shape.
why_matters: A blanket cut cannot distinguish scan-chain-present flops from genuinely non-scan flops, silently exempting scan paths (lock-up latch trap). Targeted cuts (e.g. -through [get_pins *scan*]) are the recommended pattern and never fire.
fix: Restrict the exception to genuinely non-scan flops (e.g. -to [get_cells non_scan_*]) or use mode-specific set_case_analysis. Never false-path flops present in the scan chain, even though they appear in non-scan reports.

name: Flat Derate on Advanced-Node Flow
description: The file signals an advanced (<=16nm) methodology: a small-node token in a set_operating_conditions command (e.g. SS_0P72V_16C), an explicit Nnm mention, or a POCV/AOCV/sigma keyword, yet all derates are flat single-number set_timing_derate values.
why_matters: A derate strategy correct for an older node silently persists after migration: reintroducing excess pessimism (wasted area/power on phantom violations) or insufficient margin (real risk missed). Flat OCV derate is legitimate for many blocks, hence advisory only.
fix: Consider table-based AOCV or sigma-based POCV derates for the advanced node; if flat values are intentional, add a comment explaining why the methodology was kept.

name: Derate Methodology Mix
description: Flat set_timing_derate values coexist with sigma/table-based derates (a command carrying sigma / pocv / derate_table) in one file.
why_matters: Flat and statistical/table derates are not meant to be mixed: the two methodologies answer the same question with different pessimism models, and mixing them makes results inconsistent across the design.
fix: Pick one derate methodology for the corner: either keep flat derates throughout or move to a single table/sigma-based scheme.
